title: Hiroshima Marks 81st Anniversary of Atomic Bombing Amid Nuclear Policy Debate
detail: About 50,000 people gathered at Hiroshima's Peace Memorial Park on August 6, 2026, for the 81st anniversary of the US atomic bombing that killed an estimated 140,000 people by the end of 1945. The city observed a moment of silence at 8:15 a.m., the exact time the 'Little Boy' bomb detonated. Hiroshima Mayor Kazumi Matsui warned against 'downplaying the inhumanity of nuclear weapons' and cautioned that accepting force to pursue prosperity risked triggering cycles leading to another catastrophe. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, attending the ceremony, reaffirmed Japan's Three Non-Nuclear Principles and called for continued progress toward a nuclear-free world, even as her government faces growing scrutiny over a possible policy shift; a recent poll found 76% of respondents want the principles maintained, and 128 local assemblies across 36 prefectures have urged the government to uphold them. The names of 4,393 additional victims confirmed dead over the past year were added to the park's cenotaph, bringing the total to 353,639. The number of surviving hibakusha has fallen to 91,105, roughly a quarter of the original number, with an average age exceeding 86.
